title: Our National Flag
status: draft: written 19 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 2 Environmental Activities; not yet checked by a CBC Environmental Activities teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Colour meanings as the school teaches them (black: the people; red: the blood shed for independence; green: the land; white: peace; the shield and spears: defence of freedom).

skills.key_step: The child names the colours of the Kenya flag in order and says what each stands for.

floor.question: What flies on a pole at school?

representations: a real or printed Kenya flag
steps: Name each colour from the top.
contexts: a flag at the chief's office

board.do: Draw the outline of the flag.

board.say: Which colour goes here and what does it stand for?

board.do: Wait for the child to say black, the people of Kenya.
Colour each stripe and write its meaning.

misconceptions.ask: What does red stand for on the Kenya flag?
misconceptions.repair: Tell the short story of the struggle for independence. Red remembers those who died.

misconceptions.ask: What does green stand for on the Kenya flag?
misconceptions.repair: Show pictures of farms, forests and wildlife: all part of our land.

misconceptions.ask: Which colour is at the top of the Kenya flag?
misconceptions.repair: Colour a flag strip by strip from the top, saying "black, white, red, white, green".

misconceptions.ask: What do the white stripes on our flag stand for?
misconceptions.repair: Point at each white stripe and say "peace". Ask why peace is placed between the colours.

skills.key_step: The child names occasions when the anthem is sung and shows the right behaviour when the flag is raised or lowered.
representations: a flag and a short pole
steps: Fold the flag off the ground.

board.do: Draw a child running while the flag goes up.
Wait for the child to say no, stop and stand still.
Write: stop, face the flag, stand still.

misconceptions.ask: Is the national anthem sung while playing football at break?
misconceptions.repair: List occasions on the board. Say: the anthem is for important moments.

misconceptions.ask: The flag is being raised and you are walking to class. What do you do?
misconceptions.repair: Practise in the field: when the flag goes up, everyone freezes and faces it.

misconceptions.ask: Can the flag touch the ground?
misconceptions.repair: Fold a flag in pairs, held off the ground. Say: we show it respect.

misconceptions.ask: What do you do with your hat when the anthem is sung?
misconceptions.repair: Show a picture of an assembly with caps removed. Practise.

checks.question: Name a day when the anthem is sung.
checks.answer: Jamhuri Day (Madaraka Day, Mashujaa Day, assembly)

checks.question: What do you do when the flag is raised?
checks.answer: Stop and stand still facing it
